emails.subject: Your insurance bill went up. Did your income?
emails.preheader: Did your health insurance premium suddenly jump from a few dollars to several hundred dollars a month?
emails.html:
Hi {{first_name}},

Did your health insurance premium suddenly jump from a few dollars to several hundred dollars a month?

You're not alone. Many Illinois residents are discovering that their premiums have increased dramatically, even when their income hasn't changed.

Here's why:

✓Enhanced federal Premium Tax Credits expired at the end of 2025.
✓Financial assistance available in 2026 is different from previous years.
✓Household income, family size and eligibility all affect your assistance.

A higher premium doesn't automatically mean you've run out of options.

Before accepting a higher payment or dropping coverage, have your application and available plans reviewed.

Want help? Reply to this email or text me directly at (872) 217-1852. Just send REVIEW.

emails.subject: You're paying more. But what are you actually getting?
emails.preheader: A lower monthly premium doesn't necessarily mean affordable healthcare.
emails.html:
Hi {{first_name}},

A lower monthly premium doesn't necessarily mean affordable healthcare.

Some plans come with higher deductibles, expensive specialist visits and significant out-of-pocket expenses.

Before choosing your 2027 coverage, look beyond the monthly payment:

✓Annual deductible.
✓Doctor and specialist copayments.
✓Prescription coverage.
✓Hospital and emergency room costs.
✓Maximum out-of-pocket expenses.

The cheapest plan isn't always the most affordable when you actually need medical care.

I'd be happy to help compare your available Illinois Marketplace plans.

emails.subject: Your insurance company may be leaving Georgia in 2027.
emails.preheader: If you're currently enrolled in a Cigna or UnitedHealthcare Marketplace plan, there's something important you
emails.html:
Hi {{first_name}},

If you're currently enrolled in a Cigna or UnitedHealthcare Marketplace plan, there's something important you need to know before renewing your coverage.

Both carriers are exiting Georgia's ACA Marketplace for 2027.

Your existing coverage should not be assumed to continue into next year.

Here's what you need to review:

✓Which insurance companies are available in your county for 2027?
✓Which replacement plans are available?
✓Are your current doctors and hospitals still in-network?
✓Are your prescriptions covered?
✓How will your monthly premium and deductible change?

Georgia Access will automatically re-enroll eligible consumers when their existing plan remains available, but if your insurer isn't offering plans in your area, you'll need to select new coverage.

Don't wait until January to discover you need a new insurance company.

Reply to this email or text me directly at (872) 217-1852. Just send CARRIER.

(872) 217-1852

emails.subject: Paying thousands for insurance but still can't afford to see a doctor?
emails.preheader: One of the biggest frustrations with health insurance is paying a monthly premium and still facing thousands o
emails.html:
Hi {{first_name}},

One of the biggest frustrations with health insurance is paying a monthly premium and still facing thousands of dollars in potential medical expenses.

A cheaper Bronze plan might reduce your monthly payment, but it can also come with a substantial deductible.

Before choosing your 2027 coverage, look at:

✓Annual deductible.
✓Specialist and primary care costs.
✓Prescription drug coverage.
✓Hospital and emergency room expenses.
✓Maximum out-of-pocket limits.

Remember, your deductible isn't always what you pay for every service. Some plans cover certain services before the deductible.

The goal isn't simply to find the cheapest insurance. It's to find coverage you can actually afford to use.

Want help comparing your options? Reply to this email or text me directly at (872) 217-1852. Just send COMPARE.

emails.subject: Your income changed. Did your health insurance assistance change too?
emails.preheader: Did you recently get a raise, change jobs, start working independently or experience a change in household inc
emails.html:
Hi {{first_name}},

Did you recently get a raise, change jobs, start working independently or experience a change in household income?

Your income directly affects your Marketplace financial assistance.

Many consumers don't realize that failing to update their Georgia Access application can create problems later.

Here's what you should understand:

✓Premium Tax Credits are based on estimated household income and family size.
✓Employer-sponsored coverage can affect your eligibility.
✓Changes in income should be reported promptly.
✓Your actual tax credit is reconciled when you file your taxes.

Important for 2026: If you receive more advance Premium Tax Credits than you're ultimately eligible for, the IRS generally requires repayment of the full excess amount. Previous repayment caps no longer apply.

Don't guess your income or leave outdated information on your application.

Reply to this email or text me directly at (872) 217-1852. Just send INCOME.

Donny Wilson
The Support Life
(872) 217-1852

Source: IRS – Repayment of excess advance Premium Tax Credits and IRS – Reporting changes in circumstances.

Georgia Access has changed how Georgians shop for and manage their Marketplace coverage.

Before moving forward with your 2027 coverage, verify:

✓Is your current application accurate?
✓Is your household income updated?

If you've experienced account problems, duplicate applications or unexpected enrollment changes, don't ignore them.

An enrollment mistake can become a coverage and billing problem if it's left unresolved.

emails.subject: Lost Medicaid? Let's look at your Georgia coverage options.
emails.preheader: If you've lost Medicaid, received a termination notice or been denied coverage, you may have other options wor
emails.html:
Hi {{first_name}},

If you've lost Medicaid, received a termination notice or been denied coverage, you may have other options worth exploring.

Georgia has different eligibility pathways for Medicaid, including Georgia Pathways to Coverage, as well as private Marketplace insurance through Georgia Access.

However, eligibility isn't the same for everyone.

Here's what you should understand:

✓Losing Medicaid or PeachCare for Kids may qualify you for a Special Enrollment Period.
✓Georgia Access provides a 90-day enrollment window following qualifying Medicaid or PeachCare coverage loss.
✓Georgia Pathways has separate income and community engagement requirements.
✓Not everyone who is denied Medicaid automatically qualifies for subsidized Marketplace coverage.

For 2027, Georgia Pathways eligibility requirements are also changing.

Don't assume you're ineligible for every option just because one application was denied.

If you've lost coverage or are struggling to understand your eligibility, let's review your situation.

Reply to this email or text me directly at (872) 217-1852. Just send MEDICAID.

Donny Wilson
The Support Life
(872) 217-1852

Source: Georgia Access – Special Enrollment Periods, Georgia Pathways – Eligibility and 2027 Georgia Pathways changes.

emails.preheader: Here's something many people discover the hard way:
emails.html:

A doctor who accepts one plan from an insurance company may not accept every plan from that company. Different Marketplace plans can have completely different networks.

✓Your specialists.
✓Your preferred hospitals.
✓Your prescriptions.

emails.subject: Lost Medicaid? Let's look at your {{state_name}} coverage options.
emails.preheader: If you've lost Medicaid, received a termination notice or been denied coverage, don't wait until you're uninsu
emails.html:
Hi {{first_name}},

If you've lost Medicaid, received a termination notice or been denied coverage, don't wait until you're uninsured to explore your options.

Medicaid rules are not the same in every state, so your options in {{state_name}} depend on your income and household. If you no longer qualify, private Marketplace coverage may be an option.

A few things matter:

✓When does your Medicaid coverage end?
✓What is your household income?
✓Does your employer offer health insurance?
✓When does your enrollment window close?

Losing Medicaid or CHIP may qualify you for a Special Enrollment Period, but the window is limited, so check it early.

Need help exploring your options? Reply to this email or text me directly at (872) 217-1852. Just send MEDICAID.
